faq.answer: No. Values, faith, school requirements, professional development, mutual aid, or community necessity may explain volunteering. Compare free choice, follow-through, and recognition effects.
faq.question: Does volunteering prove a social Seven subtype?

faq.answer: A stated sacrifice may benefit others, protect status, meet an imposed role, or express a chosen value. Recognition conditions help separate these explanations without assigning moral worth.
faq.question: Why examine sacrifice and recognition together?

faq.answer: Steady participation in uncredited maintenance, without resentment or a need to reopen more stimulating roles, weakens a recognition-centered account of shared possibility.
faq.question: What anonymous task weakens the social hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The tradition suggests that attention may move toward inspiring a group, postponing an immediate preference, or becoming the person who opens a better collective future. Observe who benefits and what choice remains available.
sections.title: Treat contribution as a proposed route to possibility

sections.body_md: Social instinct is used here as a traditional observation label, not evidence about bodily mechanisms. Belonging, exclusion, status, law, and organizational design require direct contextual analysis.
sections.title: Keep social language at the level of attention and roles

sections.body_md: Hold the task and group benefit constant, then compare participation when credit is public versus absent. Record whether energy, promise completion, resentment, and option seeking change with recognition.
sections.title: Compare recognized and anonymous contribution

sections.body_md: This hypothesis can include delaying pleasure for a cause as well as energizing others around a shared possibility. Neither self-denial nor charisma is sufficient without repeated context and counterexamples.
sections.title: Expect both restraint and visible enthusiasm

sections.body_md: Care work, activism, teaching, religious duty, citizenship demands, marginalized-group survival, performance metrics, and promotion systems may reward sacrifice or public contribution. These forces can be more explanatory than subtype.
sections.title: Audit unpaid labor and institutional incentives

sections.body_md: Confidence should decline when the person comfortably chooses a private preference, contributes anonymously without tracking recognition, refuses unfair service expectations, or stays with routine group maintenance after inspiration fades.
sections.title: Look for private enjoyment without moral accounting

sections.body_md: The subtype hypothesis does not measure generosity, selfishness, citizenship, leadership, or ethics. Instrument-specific evidence cannot establish universal ontology or cultural equivalence, and group consequences remain factual questions.
sections.title: Do not infer virtue or universal structure

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Across five days, select one visible contribution and one anonymous maintenance task that offer comparable benefit to the same group.

Observable signal: Record promised work, actual beneficiary, personal preference deferred, recognition available, resentment stated, completion quality, and freedom to decline.

Page-specific signal: Compare engagement when status is removed but the collective benefit and workload remain similar.

Alternative explanation: Check unpaid role expectations, care duties, faith practice, activism, promotion incentives, exclusion risk, and community survival needs.

Reflection prompt: Identify whether recognition, free choice, or concrete group benefit best explains the difference and revise the subtype claim accordingly.

seo.description: Type Seven social is a traditional, evidence-limited hypothesis combining Type Seven possibility with contribution, shared possibility, group ideals, and tension around recognition. Service or sacrifice does not establish subtype because unpaid labor, professional duty, community survival, status incentives, discrimination, and role expectations can create similar behavior.
seo.title: Type Seven social: a contribution, shared possibility, and recognition tension hypothesis
